the shear viscosity to entropy ratio is approximately constant when going to higher energies and when changing the saturation scale Q_s.

the shear viscosity over entropy density of a quark gluon plasma created in heavy ion collisions is close to the lower bound predicted by AdS/CFT, and that this lower bound is saturated by the quark gluon plasmas created in heavy ion experiments.

(i) the shear viscosity to entropy ratio of the QGP at LHC energies is similar to the one at RHIC energies; (ii) the ratio eta/s decreases by a factor 2.5 when increasing the saturation momentum Q_s by a factor 4, and (iii) eta/s is independent of the initial temperature T_i for temperatures T_i > 300 MeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the shear viscosity to entropy ratio within a microscopic transport approach.
the study of the shear viscosity to entropy ratio eta/s within a perturbative kinetic approach.
the study of the shear viscosity of strongly interacting matter in the framework of a perturbative parton cascade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shear viscosity to entropy ratio of the QCD medium is of the order 0.15.
the entropy is not a good probe of QGP viscosity, because it is dominated by the entropy produced in the initial stages of the collision, which is not well known.
the shear viscosity is of the same magnitude as the entropy density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the shear viscosity is a universal quantity in the parton phase.
the shear viscosity to entropy ratio is not sensitive to the initial saturation momentum scale.
the shear viscosity to entropy ratio of a QCD matter at RHIC and LHC is approximately the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy production in the initial state is not negligible.
the entropy production in the initial state is the main driver for the shear viscosity.
the shear viscosity to entropy ratio is a constant in the regime where hydrodynamic behavior is valid.
